guidelineReference: Resus Council UK Adult Basic Life Support 2021
title: Unresponsive poisoning at an evening carnival
setting: Carnival procession. You find a patient collapsed on the grass. Scattered beer cans/bottles are on the ground, and she has vomited. Responding only with groans.
verdictExplanation: Unresponsive, groaning only, compromised airway from vomit, hypothermia (35°C), and respiratory depression. Sick: protect airway and call 999.

shared.danger: Broken glass bottles and vomit on the floor
shared.response: Responding to voice only with groans, level of consciousness dropping
shared.circulation: Bradycardic, extremely cold and pale skin

history.history: Found collapsed on the ground by stewards. History of heavy drinking.
history.additional: Found lying in a puddle of vomit on the damp ground

followUp.question: What is the priority first aid intervention for this patient?

options.text: Clear the airway of vomit, place in the recovery position, cover with a space blanket, and call 999
Attempt to induce further vomiting by placing a finger down her throat
Administer oral glucose gel to treat suspected low blood sugar
Force her to sit upright on a chair and keep her moving

followUp.explanation: Positioning in the recovery position is critical to prevent aspiration of vomit. Covering her with a blanket treats her hypothermia (35.0°C). Inducing vomiting is dangerous and causes airway obstruction. Do not give anything by mouth to an unresponsive patient.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Protect the airway in the recovery position. Keep her warm using blankets. Call 999 immediately.
levelFlags.erNotes: Unresponsive breathing patient with hypothermia. Maintain recovery position, clear airway, give high-flow oxygen, check BGL, actively rewarm, and transfer rapidly.
